title: Apple Pie
description: The kind of pie that disappears faster than good intentions — crisp pastry, soft spiced apples, and zero leftovers.

method.instruction: Peel, core, and slice the apples evenly.
Place apples, sugar, cloves, and water into a saucepan. Simmer gently over medium heat until apples are just tender, about 8–10 minutes. Set aside to cool completely.
Sift plain flour, self-raising flour, and custard powder into a bowl. Rub in chilled butter until the mixture resembles fine breadcrumbs.
Add cold water gradually, mixing until the dough just comes together. Do not overwork. Wrap and refrigerate for 15 minutes.
Divide dough into two portions. Roll out one portion and line a greased 23cm pie tin.
Fill with cooled apple mixture. Roll out remaining dough, cover pie, seal and crimp edges. Brush with a little milk or egg wash.
Bake at 180°C for 40–45 minutes until golden and crisp. Rest for 10 minutes before slicing.

notes.title: Serving Tip
notes.content: Serve warm with cream, custard, or vanilla ice cream.

notes.title: Pastry Tip
notes.content: Keep the butter cold and handle the dough as little as possible for a shorter, flakier pastry. A food processor makes this easier — pulse the butter into the flour until it resembles breadcrumbs, then add cold water gradually until the dough just comes together.
